## Integrating Cast AI metrics with New Relic   [Skip link to Integrating Cast AI metrics with New Relic](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#integrating-cast-ai-metrics-with-new-relic)

This guide explains how to integrate Cast AI metrics with New Relic using Prometheus, allowing you to visualize and analyze your cluster metrics alongside other observability data.

### Prerequisites   [Skip link to Prerequisites](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#prerequisites)

Before starting the integration, ensure you have:

- Access to your Kubernetes cluster with sufficient permissions
- Helm CLI installed
- `kubectl` CLI installed
- A New Relic account and license key
- Basic familiarity with Prometheus and Kubernetes concepts

### Install Prometheus   [Skip link to Install Prometheus](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#install-prometheus)

If you don't already have Prometheus installed in your cluster, follow these steps:

1. Add the Prometheus Helm repository:

Shell

```shell
helm repo add prometheus-community https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts
helm repo update
```

2. Install Prometheus using Helm:

Shell

```shell
helm install prometheus prometheus-community/prometheus \
  --namespace monitoring \
  --create-namespace
```

### Install New Relic integration   [Skip link to Install New Relic integration](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#install-new-relic-integration)

1. Install the New Relic CLI following the instructions at [New Relic CLI documentation](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/infrastructure/install-infrastructure-agent/linux-installation/install-infrastructure-monitoring-agent-linux/)

2. Add the New Relic Helm repository:


Shell

```shell
helm repo add newrelic https://helm-charts.newrelic.com
helm repo update
```

3. Install the New Relic Kubernetes integration:

Shell

```shell
helm install newrelic newrelic/nri-bundle \
  --set global.licenseKey=<YOUR_LICENSE_KEY> \
  --namespace newrelic \
  --create-namespace \
  --set global.cluster=<cluster_name>
```

4. Verify the installation and check if New Relic pods are running after this.

Shell

```shell
kubectl get pods -n newrelic
```

### Configure Prometheus to scrape Cast AI metrics   [Skip link to Configure Prometheus to scrape Cast AI metrics](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#configure-prometheus-to-scrape-cast-ai-metrics)

Modify your Prometheus configuration to collect Cast AI metrics by editing the Prometheus ConfigMap. Add the following scrape configuration:

YAML

```yaml
scrape_configs:
 - job_name: 'castai_cluster_metrics'
   scrape_interval: 15s
   scheme: https
   static_configs:
     - targets: ['$CASTAI_API_URL']
   metrics_path: '/v1/metrics/prom'
   authorization:
     type: 'Token'
     credentials: '{apiKey}'
```

Replace `{apiKey}` with your Cast AI API token. You can add multiple jobs to this section; please refer to [Prometheus and Grafana](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/prometheus-and-grafana#how-to-visualize-cast-ai-metrics-in-prometheus-and-grafana).

After updating the configuration, restart the Prometheus server pod:

Shell

```shell
kubectl delete pod -l app=prometheus-server -n monitoring
```

> 📘
>
> ### Note   [Skip link to Note](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#note)
>
> If you encounter YAML formatting errors when updating the ConfigMap, ensure proper indentation in your configuration. Common errors include incorrect spacing or missing keys. Refer to [Kubernetes documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/configmap/).

### Verify metric collection   [Skip link to Verify metric collection](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#verify-metric-collection)

1. Port forward the Prometheus server to verify metric collection:

Shell

```shell
kubectl port-forward svc/prometheus-server 9090:80 -n monitoring
```

2. Open `http://localhost:9090/targets` in your browser, verify that the Cast AI jobs are listed and showing the `UP` status.

![](https://files.readme.io/be99382df43d19ef8d1589e2775e95ae1bc736a8247b27d3210aea1c7100741b-image.png)


### Configure New Relic remote write integration   [Skip link to Configure New Relic remote write integration](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#configure-new-relic-remote-write-integration)

To send metrics from Prometheus to New Relic:

1. Navigate to the _Integrations & Agents_ section in your New Relic dashboard

2. Select _Prometheus Remote Write Integration_ and click _Begin Installation_

![](https://files.readme.io/3d37e235b7d5f2968167b0b3d161a36cbf885f8504d0ced8700a137996218c03-image.png)

3. Configure the remote write integration:

a. Enter a name for your data source


b. Generate or select an existing API key

![](https://files.readme.io/7391cfa54d2ebf1379a262847f0e7b3f9a47bc6c60cc70c1dbf802a62a6f19e0-image.png)

4. Copy the provided `remote_write` URL and add the remote write configuration to your Prometheus ConfigMap:

![](https://files.readme.io/41bd0ce5a3a40875322170c367fe3bf7a1aefe347cf86f4829432c3702a46122-image.png)


The format is as follows, as shown in the above screenshot:

YAML

```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: https://metric-api.newrelic.com/prometheus/v1/write?prometheus_server=YOUR_DATA_SOURCE_NAME
    authorization:
      credentials: YOUR_LICENSE_KEY
```

5. Restart the Prometheus server pod to apply the changes:

Shell

```shell
kubectl delete pod -l app=prometheus-server -n monitoring
```

### Verify data in New Relic   [Skip link to Verify data in New Relic](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#verify-data-in-new-relic)

1. Navigate to the _Dashboards_ section in New Relic

![](https://files.readme.io/1b248b45379b4f817d8de8294e794b3507db45088734232ede9475790efba8c1-image.png)

2. Confirm that your Prometheus data source is visible and metrics are streaming

3. You can now create custom dashboards and alerts using Cast AI metrics in New Relic


### Available metrics   [Skip link to Available metrics](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#available-metrics)

For a complete list of available metrics and their descriptions, refer to our [metrics documentation](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/prometheus-and-grafana).

### Troubleshooting   [Skip link to Troubleshooting](https://docs.cast.ai/docs/observability-metrics-integrating-prometheus-metrics-with-new-relic\#troubleshooting)

If you encounter issues:

1. Verify Prometheus scrape targets are working:

Shell

```shell
kubectl port-forward svc/prometheus-server 9090:80 -n monitoring
```

Then check `http://localhost:9090/targets`

2. Check Prometheus server logs:

Shell

```shell
kubectl logs -l app=prometheus-server -n monitoring
```

3. Verify New Relic integration pods are running:

Shell

```shell
kubectl get pods -n newrelic
```

4. For configuration errors, ensure proper YAML formatting and indentation in your Prometheus ConfigMap

For additional support, contact Cast AI support or refer to [New Relic's Prometheus documentation](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/infrastructure/prometheus-integrations/get-started/send-prometheus-metric-data-new-relic/).
